rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: **Alkyl groups.** An alkyl group is an alkane minus one hydrogen — methyl (CH₃—), ethyl (C₂H₅—), propyl (C₃H₇—) — with the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₁.  ·  **Functional group.** An atom or group that determines a compound's characteristic reactions, such as —OH (alcohol), —CHO (aldehyde), —COOH (carboxylic acid) and —NH₂ (amine).

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Homologous series.** A series whose members share a general formula, differ by a CH₂ (14 u) unit, show similar chemical properties and a gradual trend in physical properties.  ·  **IUPAC naming.** Names combine a prefix (substituents), a word root (carbon count: meth-, eth-, prop-) and a suffix (-ane, -ene, -yne, -ol, -al, -oic acid).  ·  **Example.** The alkanes methane through pentane form one homologous series; boiling point rises with chain length and branching lowers it at the same carbon count.
